newsitem.title: CHILE: Latin American shares seen cooling off this week.
newsitem.headline: Latin American shares seen cooling off this week.

text.p: Latin American stocks will probably take a breather this week from record-breaking rallies on bourses across the region, brokers and analysts said.
Although the general bullish feeling was likely to continue, especially with Wall Street surging, profit-taking will probably temper the gains this week, they said.

"This week we'll start seeing some resistance. The market went up too fast and some people need to take their profits," said a broker at the Santiago Stock Exchange, summing up sentiment on trading floors throughout the region.

Brokers said Chilean shares could yet add to last week's gains but at a more measured pace and with some profit-taking likely early in the week. Santiago's selective .IPSA index rose 4.2 percent last week to end Friday at 136.14 points, with electricity shares leading the way on strong foreign buying.
In Mexico, analysts said profit-takers were likely to step in after a record-breaking streak last week, in which the IPC index .MXX ended the week 2.01 percent higher at 4244.63 points.

Analysts in Mexico noted that big institutional investors were quick to take profits during Friday's session and said Wall Street investors may pull back in the runup to Mexico's mid-term elections on July 6.
But profit-taking would still probably be limited and support should stand at about 4,200 points, technical analysts said.
Venezuela's bullish trend is likely to continue this week although again interspersed with rough patches of profit-taking, traders said.
"Technically there should be a round of profit-taking, but so long as the New York Stock Exchange keeps rising so too should the Caracas bolsa," said Banesco broker Simon Brad in Caracas.

The 19-share .IBC Caracas index ended four percent higher for the week on Friday at 7,535.54 points, propelled by last week's approval of important labor market reforms and a recent round of oil auctions that netted the country $2.1 billion in bids.

Brazilian stocks were also expected to post new gains this week, motivated by increasing capital influx, but the first three sessions may be volatile as options settle Monday and futures index contracts are liquidated on Wednesday.
As in Chile, electrical shares in Sao Paulo are expected to continue bolstering the market as investors take advantage of the sector's upside potential.
Investors will be also be watching for a vote in Congress on a general telecommunications law setting rules for privatization of the telecom industry.
Sao Paulo's Bovespa selective index .BVSP rose 4.3 percent to 11,828 points, bringing the rise so far this year to a heady 68 percent.
The trading week in Argentina will be shortened by Monday's Flag Day holiday. Stocks were expected to keep their firm tone when trading reopens Tuesday, dealers said.
"The market is underpinned by a combination of excellent local economic fundamentals and the bull run on Wall Street, which shows interest rates are fading," said Gabriel Ruiz at brokers Tavelli.
He expected prices to push higher this week, with steady buying for foreign investors, although they could stay rangebound in the first couple of sessions as the market consolidates recent gains.
Friday's options expirations could also put some pressure on blue chips.
The selective Merval index .MERV rose 1.3 percent last week to 813.40 points at Friday's close.
